# Pylon

> Pusher-protocol-compatible WebSocket server in Rust, a single static binary, drop-in for Pusher Channels, soketi or Laravel Reverb behind unchanged Pusher SDKs. Built by the team behind ThriveDesk (https://www.thrivedesk.com), the AI-powered helpdesk for ecommerce and SaaS teams.

Pylon's recommended production deployment is a Linux host under systemd: install the single static binary at `/usr/local/bin/pylon`, run it as a dedicated `pylon` system user, and configure it with one environment file (`/etc/pylon/pylon.env`) and one apps file (`/etc/pylon/apps.json`). Apply the `systemd/99-pylon.sysctl.conf` kernel-tuning drop-in shipped in the release tarball once per host. TLS terminates either natively in pylon (`PYLON_TLS_CERT` / `PYLON_TLS_KEY`) or behind a reverse proxy such as nginx or Caddy. Pylon listens on port 7000 by default and exposes a liveness probe at `/health` and a readiness probe at `/ready`. Docker and Kubernetes are alternatives, covered below under Optional.

Minimal install on a systemd host:

```bash
# Replace X.Y.Z and ARCH (x86_64 or aarch64) as appropriate.
# Note the asset name carries the leading "v" of the tag.
ASSET=pylon-vX.Y.Z-ARCH-unknown-linux-musl

curl -LO "https://github.com/i-rocky/pylon/releases/download/vX.Y.Z/${ASSET}.tar.gz"
curl -LO "https://github.com/i-rocky/pylon/releases/download/vX.Y.Z/${ASSET}.tar.gz.sha256"

sha256sum -c "${ASSET}.tar.gz.sha256"
tar xzf "${ASSET}.tar.gz"

# The tarball unpacks into a directory containing the binary plus
# LICENSE, README.md, apps.example.json, and a systemd/ directory with
# pylon.service, pylon.env.example and 99-pylon.sysctl.conf.
"./${ASSET}/pylon" --version

cp "./${ASSET}/systemd/99-pylon.sysctl.conf" /etc/sysctl.d/
sysctl --system

# Create the system user.
useradd --system --no-create-home --shell /sbin/nologin pylon

# Install the binary.
install -m 0755 "./${ASSET}/pylon" /usr/local/bin/pylon

# Create the config directory (owned root, readable by pylon group).
install -d -m 0750 -o root -g pylon /etc/pylon

# Install and edit the environment file.
install -m 0640 -o root -g pylon \
    "./${ASSET}/systemd/pylon.env.example" /etc/pylon/pylon.env
# Edit /etc/pylon/pylon.env — set adapter, Redis URL, etc.

# Install the apps config.
install -m 0640 -o root -g pylon \
    "./${ASSET}/apps.example.json" /etc/pylon/apps.json
# IMPORTANT: change the "secret" field in apps.json.

# Install the systemd unit.
cp "./${ASSET}/systemd/pylon.service" /etc/systemd/system/
systemctl daemon-reload

systemctl enable --now pylon

# Health check
curl -s http://localhost:7000/health
curl -s http://localhost:7000/ready
```

## Install and run

- [Installation](https://i-rocky.github.io/pylon/user-guide/installation/): OS requirements (Linux amd64/arm64, statically linked musl binaries) and installing via Docker, a prebuilt binary, or building from source.
- [Quick Start](https://i-rocky.github.io/pylon/user-guide/quick-start/): Gets Pylon running locally and verifies it works end-to-end using a Pusher client SDK and a Pusher server SDK.
- [Deployment](https://i-rocky.github.io/pylon/user-guide/deployment/): Deploy artifacts for three targets — bare metal/systemd, Docker/Compose, and Kubernetes/Helm.
- [Configuration](https://i-rocky.github.io/pylon/user-guide/configuration/): The two configuration layers — the application store (`apps.json` or a database) and `PYLON_*` environment variables.
- [TLS / SSL](https://i-rocky.github.io/pylon/user-guide/tls/): Two approaches for adding TLS — a reverse proxy (nginx or Caddy) or pylon's native TLS.
- [Production Tuning](https://i-rocky.github.io/pylon/user-guide/production-tuning/): OS-level and pylon-specific settings to maximise connection density and reliability in production.
- [Applications & Authentication](https://i-rocky.github.io/pylon/user-guide/applications/): The application registry — multiple applications per server, each with its own key/secret pair, defined in `apps.json`.

## Use it

- [Connecting Clients](https://i-rocky.github.io/pylon/user-guide/clients/): Pylon speaks the Pusher Channels v7 WebSocket protocol, so any Pusher-compatible client SDK works against it unchanged.
- [Triggering Events](https://i-rocky.github.io/pylon/user-guide/triggering-events/): Server-side code triggers events by calling the Pusher HTTP API, via an official server SDK or raw signed HTTP requests.
- [Channels](https://i-rocky.github.io/pylon/user-guide/channels/): All Pusher Channels v7 channel types — the channel name prefix determines its type and required authentication.
- [Webhooks](https://i-rocky.github.io/pylon/user-guide/webhooks/): Signed HTTP POST webhooks fired to your server on channel events, configured per-app in `apps.json`, retried for up to five minutes.

## Operate

- [Observability](https://i-rocky.github.io/pylon/user-guide/observability/): Prometheus metrics, a liveness probe, and a readiness probe on the same HTTP port as the REST API (default 7000).
- [Troubleshooting & FAQ](https://i-rocky.github.io/pylon/user-guide/troubleshooting/): The numeric close codes pylon sends before closing a WebSocket connection, plus other troubleshooting and FAQ topics.

## Optional

- [Clustering & Scaling](https://i-rocky.github.io/pylon/user-guide/clustering/): Pylon scales horizontally by connecting multiple nodes through a shared Redis instance; each node is stateless from a routing perspective.
- [Architecture](https://i-rocky.github.io/pylon/dev-guide/architecture/): Pylon is a single Rust binary built around a lock-free, per-core transport; describes the major subsystems and how data flows through them.
- [Pusher Protocol Reference](https://i-rocky.github.io/pylon/dev-guide/protocol/): The Pusher Channels protocol v7 wire details pylon enforces, for contributors and integration authors.
- [Building & Testing](https://i-rocky.github.io/pylon/dev-guide/building-and-testing/): The Rust toolchain is pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml`; rustup reads it automatically on a fresh checkout.
- [Contributing](https://i-rocky.github.io/pylon/dev-guide/contributing/): A summary of the key contribution expectations; full guidelines are in `CONTRIBUTING.md` at the repository root.
- [Release Process](https://i-rocky.github.io/pylon/dev-guide/release-process/): Releases are tag-driven — pushing a `vX.Y.Z` tag triggers the GitHub Actions release workflow that builds native binaries and a multi-arch container image.
